citation: Simmons, D. C., Coyne, M. D., Hagan-Burke, S., Kwok, O., Simmons, L., Johnson, C., Zou, Y., Taylor, A. B., McAlenney, A. L., Ruby, M., & Crevecoeur, Y. C. (2011). Effects of supplemental reading interventions in authentic contexts: A comparison of kindergarteners' response. Exceptional Children, 77(2), 207-228. https://doi.org/10.1177/001440291107700204
report_number: Journal article (no IES/NCEE/EEF report number). DOI: 10.1177/001440291107700204. ERIC: EJ918891. Part of IES Project Early Reading Intervention. The replication of the same ERI intervention by overlapping authors is Coyne et al. 2013 (J. Research on Educational Effectiveness, DOI 10.1080/19345747.2012.706694).
design: Cluster-randomized RCT; assignment at the interventionist/classroom level (Teacher/Class) within school; 12 schools (TX N=4, CT N=8); 57 intervention groups/interventionists (31 ERI experimental, 26 TPI comparison); 206 kindergarteners (K, K-2 band) identified as at risk for reading difficulty completed pre+post; ~100 sessions, 30 min/day, 5 days/week, small groups of 3-5; subject = early reading (Reading). Analysis = HLM (HLM 6.04, REML) with pretest, PPVT, age, gender, ethnicity, special-ed, bilingual covariates and school treated as a fixed factor (11 dummies); Hedges (2007) cluster-randomized effect size (delta_T) reported in Table 4. Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied.
problems: ACTIVE COMPARISON CONDITION, NOT BUSINESS-AS-USUAL. The contrast extracted (row 108) is ERI (explicit/systematic commercial code-based supplemental program) vs TPI = 'typical practice intervention', which is itself an ACTIVE school-designed supplemental small-group reading intervention delivered for equal time (30 min/day), equal group sizes (3-5), and by comparable school personnel. The authors are explicit (Methods p.211: 'To equate for extraneous variables, comparison group students were taught in similar-sized groups of three to five for similar amounts of time, rather than a no-treatment control'; Discussion p.224 & Summary p.225: 'instead of a no-treatment control or the general classroom reading curriculum, we compared ERI to school-designed typical practice intervention'; 'we must be cautious when interpreting effect sizes from studies that compare interventions to no-treatment controls'). The meta-analysis required business-as-usual (no alternative treatment) controls; this study does NOT meet that criterion, so all effect sizes here represent ERI vs an active alternative intervention and may need exclusion or special handling in central review. Additionally, the TPD here is only ~2 days of training for ERI interventionists (and the TPI comparison interventionists received NO professional development from the study), so the 'TPD' label and the BAU-control requirement are both questionable for this study. Comparison-specific note: TPI interventionists could (and some did) use commercial code-based programs (Saxon Phonics, SRA/Open Court, Lindamood-Bell, etc.), making the comparison an active code-instruction condition. Effect sizes (delta_T) taken directly from Table 4 (p.219), which are Hedges (2007) cluster-robust standardized mean differences (positive favors ERI); these already account for clustering and pretest/covariate/school adjustment. g_se derived as delta_T/t (delta_T and the reported t-statistic share the numerator gamma01; df=44 for all). Posttest SDs in Table 3 are raw (unadjusted) and were NOT used to standardize, because the paper's delta_T uses the model-based sqrt(sigma^2 + tau00) denominator.
